subject: QBR health check: engineering 'needles' & sprint-to-launch action log
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR health check: engineering 'needles' & sprint-to-launch action log

Team —

As we lock the QBR deck this week, I want a concise, auditable list of the top delivery risks across product + eng that could materially change our launch timeline or OKR delivery. Please treat this as the single source for the leadership readout.

Ask: by EOD Tuesday (9/15) — send one-line status + current confidence (Green/Yellow/Red) + proposed mitigation and owner. I started a spreadsheet and attached a snapshot; please add rows for any dependencies you own.

Key areas I'm tracking:
- Runtime performance targets for hosted API (not hitting tail-latency SLOs in Canary).
- Model-onboarding delays (quantization and kernel tuning backlog).
- Autoscaler behavior under burst traffic for Dedicated pools.
- Cross-team dependency: infra team needs signed infra config for Private rollout.

I'll collate and highlight any items that need exec attention for the QBR. If you think a quick shiproom is warranted, flag it.

Thanks
Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr_engineering_health_snapshot.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), sprint_to_launch_timeline.xlsx (xlsx, 200KB)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR health check: engineering 'needles' & sprint-to-launch action log

Marcus —

Quick statuses from Product/Platform side:

1) Tail latency (Hosted API) — Yellow. Canary shows median ok but 99th p spikes on sequences >2k tokens under burst. Root cause looks like the current batching heuristic + kernel selection for long sequences.
   - Mitigation: Temporary conservative batching policy for Canary (reduce max batch size) + schedule kernel swap for long-seq path. Owner: lauren_bishop.

2) Model onboarding backlog — Yellow/Red depending on model. MPT-variant we planned to ship is delayed; quantization QA failing one regression test.
   - Mitigation: Re-prioritize quantization job to unblock the MPT path; fallback: ship FP16 variant for initial launch. Owner: karthik_iyer (infra/ops) + product validation.

3) Autoscaler — Green. Stress test last week passed; we'll keep monitoring.

I've added rows in the spreadsheet (see link). Will update the confidence score by EOD.

-L
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product

Folks —

Adding a dependency note that needs immediate visibility: the quantization toolchain upgrade (QTool v2.1) is gated on the CUDA patch CVE we requested last week. Platform security needs the patch signed off by SRE and Security before we can roll v2.1 across our Dedicated fleet. If the sign-off slips, model-onboarding for 2 models slips 2-3 sprints.

My recommendation: short approval window with a rollback plan. I've documented the impact matrix in dependency_matrix.csv and added a suggested approval checklist. Owner: karthik_iyer for the rollout; security/sre for sign-off.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR health check: engineering 'needles' & sprint-to-launch action log

All —

I've sketched a contingency lane for the long-seq tail-latency issue:
- Immediate: apply conservative batching heuristic in Canary (runtime config change). Rollback in 30m if not showing perf regression. Owner: tessa_morgan.
- Short-term (3 days): integrate alternative kernel (vendor patch) into Canary images for long sequences; perf test and compare. Owner: infra engs (karthik).
- Medium-term: add a routing rule to prefer lower-latency model variant for user-facing routes when predicted sequence lengths >1.5k tokens (product config). Owner: lauren_bishop.

I've attached the timeline slice to sprint_to_launch_timeline.xlsx. I propose a 30-minute shiproom tomorrow 9/16 @ 10:00 to approve the Canary config change and decide runbooks.

Tessa
Sr. Eng Manager — Serving Runtime

Attachment: dependency_matrix.csv (csv, 12KB)

Subject: Re: QBR health check: engineering 'needles' & sprint-to-launch action log

Morning —

Quick updates after the perf run and Security sync:
- Canary batching policy applied last night (tuned max batch size to 12). 24h observations: 99th p reduced ~18% for long sequences; no regression on median. Confidence: Green->Yellow.
- Security responded on CVE patch: sign-off requested a documented rollback path and smoke tests. We're provisioning a targeted run tomorrow morning. If Security signs off, we can proceed with QTool v2.1 rollout in a controlled window (Owner: karthik_iyer).

Agreed on the shiproom 9/16 @10:00. I'll bring metrics and the smoke-test checklist.

-Hannah
Engineering Program Lead

Thanks — solid updates and the spreadsheet looks good.

Outcomes for leadership readout:
- Tail-latency: Yellow -> include mitigation (conservative batching + kernel roadmap) and note shiproom decision.
- Model onboarding: Yellow; present fallback (FP16 rollout) and quantization sign-off path tied to security timeline.
- Autoscaler: Green.

Hannah — please capture the shiproom minutes and decision (ship/hold) in the spreadsheet and drop into the QBR folder. Lauren — please prepare a one-slide impact + fallback table for the QBR. Karthik/Tessa — add owners and ETA cells to the dependency matrix.

If anything materially changes after shiproom, flag to me and I'll escalate. Otherwise I'll fold this into the executive QBR pack tonight.

Marcus
VP Engineering
